subject: SLA variance request — 99th percentile latency spike on model v8.2-quant
messages:
From: Tom Redding <tom@suncrestbank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: Suncrest Bank Ops <ops@suncrestbank.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Abrupt 99th percentile latency spike on model v8.2-quant — urgent

Stephanie / Ben —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency for the enterprise inference calls backed by model v8.2-quant at ~08:45 PDT. Our frontend graphs show 99th percentile rising from ~180ms to ~1.6s across multiple regions. This is impacting our real-time risk-scoring flows and causing timeouts.

We switched a small percentage of traffic to the pinned model v7.9.2 which reduced errors but the traffic routing is manual and fragile. Can Redwood authorize an immediate failover or provide a formal SLA variance while you investigate? Our renewal is in-flight and we need to avoid broader customer impact.

I attached a short trace capture and the error counts. Please advise next steps and expected time-to-stable.

Tom Redding
Head of Platform Operations
Suncrest Bank

Attachments: suncrest_latency_traces_20280725.zip
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.example>
To: Tom Redding <tom@suncrestbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt 99th percentile latency spike on model v8.2-quant — urgent

Tom —

Thanks for the traces and the quick mitigation you already started. We're treating this as a high-priority SLO incident and will coordinate a temporary SLA variance while we investigate.

Ben / Markus / Grace — looping you in: can product/eng confirm an actionable rollback or traffic-split plan? Markus, can you review traces and propose a recommended short-term routing (e.g., split to v7.9.2) and an estimate for a safe remediation window? Grace / Ben: I'll need a short customer note and the SLA-variance form completed if we are going to grant a temporary concession.

Tom — I'll summarize the mitigation and an approval window once we have engineering's proposal. For now we are ok to authorize an emergency traffic-shift to v7.9.2 (manual) if it reduces error rate, but we need a formal variance for 72 hours to cover any regressions while we push fixes. Please confirm you accept that window.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-variance-request-form.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt 99th percentile latency spike on model v8.2-quant — urgent

Stephanie / team —

I pulled the traces. Summary: after the v8.2-quant variant was promoted in last night's rollout, we see a kernel selection mismatch for certain sequence lengths when running on our quantized execution path for T4-like instances. The hot set of requests with short contexts (~8-16 tokens) is hitting a slower code path due to an edge-case in the attention kernel that increases compute time for those shards.

Immediate remediation plan (timeline ~90–120 minutes):
- Initiate a 70/30 traffic split routing 70% -> v7.9.2 (stable) and 30% -> v8.2-quant with logging enabled. This reduces customer-visible tail latency while preserving signal for debugging.
- Deploy a runtime micro-patch to skip the slow kernel for short contexts; this is low-risk but requires validating on canary (30 min rollout, 30 min observation).
- If the micro-patch shows regressions, we will roll forward a rollback to v7.9.2 for 100% traffic (expected ~15 min impact to routing as we reconfigure).

I'll attach the filtered traces and a short runbook. I recommend we authorize the requested 72-hour SLA variance while we validate the micro-patch.

Markus Klein
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: filtered_traces_short_contexts.log (referenced inside suncrest_latency_traces_20280725.zip)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.example>
To: Tom Redding <tom@suncrestbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, Suncrest Bank Ops <ops@suncrestbank.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Action approved: temporary SLA variance (72 hours) + traffic-split plan

Tom —

Thanks for the quick signal and for standing by while we triaged. Per internal review, Redwood will approve a temporary SLA variance for Suncrest Bank for up to 72 hours starting now (2028-07-25T12:48:00-07:00), scoped to the v8.2-quant variant. Conditions:
- We will put a 70/30 split (70% traffic to v7.9.2, 30% to v8.2-quant with debug logging) immediately.
- Our engineering team will attempt a micro-patch canary; if we see no regressions we will re-evaluate removing the variance early.
- If the micro-patch fails validation, we will perform a full rollback to v7.9.2 and notify you.

Next steps for you: please confirm acceptance of the 72-hour window and sign the attached variance form (we sent a DocuSign link). I'll have Grace draft a short external-facing note for your stakeholders. Ben will update the HubSpot deal and include the incident notes.

We realize this is sensitive during your renewal; our priority is stability and transparency.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
